evidence.why: Shared initialization, quantization loading and frame/scan parsing.
Six-block reconstruction, full-region traversal and nominal size return.
Rounded destination stride and unconditionally complete region writes.

facts.rationale: Preserves the established pipeline while correcting the assertion that the returned count always equals destination bytes produced.
facts.value: Stores src and size in shared stream state, resets three DC predictors and the entropy-bit cache, and loads two 64-entry quantization tables through the zigzag map. SOF0 supplies dimensions and SOS locates entropy data. Each 16-by-16 region reconstructs four luma blocks with the first quantizer and one Cb plus one Cr block with the second: entropy decoding, dequantization and inverse transformation precede tiled RGB565 output. The normal return is the nominal width * height * 2 image size, not a measurement of bytes written; the output helper rounds the width stride to 16 pixels and writes complete edge regions without clipping.

evidence.why: Unused height, rounded width stride and full MCU output.
Recovery zero and incompletely checked marker/payload accesses.
Dimension-controlled traversal, nominal return and public signature.

facts.rationale: Corrects the unpadded allocation guarantee and the implication that all parsing or entropy failures are detected and returned as zero.
facts.value: Concrete signature: s32 (char* src, s32 size, void* dst). src and size initialize compressed-input cursor and bound state; dst is caller-owned writable storage for tiled RGB565 output. For positive dimensions, complete 16-by-16 regions require storage accommodating the width and height rounded up to 16 pixels, at two bytes per pixel; no destination-capacity argument or edge clipping is present. Normal completion returns nominal decoded_width * decoded_height * 2, while the setjmp recovery path returns 0. Zero dimensions can also produce a normal zero return, and malformed input is not comprehensively validated.
